draft.title: Area between two curves
card: To find the area between two curves, subtract the lower function from the upper one, then integrate. Area = ∫ (upper − lower) dx.
The limits are where the curves meet. Set f(x) = g(x) and solve for x to find them.
Check which curve is on top between the limits, for example by testing a point. Subtracting the wrong way gives a negative area.
Example: y = x and y = x² meet where x = x², so at x = 0 and x = 1. Between them x is on top. Area = ∫ from 0 to 1 of (x − x²) dx = [x²/2 − x³/3] from 0 to 1 = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6.
draft.remember: Area between curves = integral of (upper − lower), from one intersection to the next.

a.q: Which integral gives the area between y = x and y = x² from x = 0 to x = 1, where y = x is the upper curve?
a.why: The area is the upper function minus the lower one, and y = x is on top, so the integrand is x − x². Using x² − x gives the right size with the wrong sign, a negative answer.
a.clue: Take the lower curve away from the upper curve.

b.q: The line y = 4 and the curve y = x² meet at x = −2 and x = 2, with the line on top. What is the area between them?
b.why: Area = ∫ from −2 to 2 of (4 − x²) dx = [4x − x³/3] from −2 to 2 = (8 − 8/3) − (−8 + 8/3) = 32/3. Using only 0 to 2 gives 16/3, which is just half of the area.
b.clue: The region runs from x = −2 to x = 2, not from 0.

check.summary: No problems found. The card, example and both answers check out: ∫₀¹(x − x²)dx = 1/6 and ∫₋₂²(4 − x²)dx = 32/3.
